title: Latency-induced decision degradation in real-time football analytics: Redis Streams vs Apache Kafka on StatsBomb open data

creators.name: Ricou, Gustavo Pedro
creators.affiliation: School of Computer Science and Statistics, Trinity College Dublin, Dublin, Ireland

description:
Code, replay plans, analysis and manuscript for a study of whether streaming-infrastructure latency degrades in-play football decisions.

Measured Apache Kafka vs Redis Streams event-delivery latency is coupled to a calibrated in-play win-probability model through the Age-of-Information lens, yielding a decision-staleness metric in probability-seconds per match. On a fair, artifact-free corpus in which each concurrent feed carries a distinct real match, the two backends are statistically equivalent (TOST against a one-broadcast-frame margin) at every concurrency level tested, and a goal's win probability is stale by about 0.014 probability-seconds regardless of backend. Redis's single-thread serialization is real but only appears near 2,100 events/second, equivalent to roughly 4,800 simultaneous real-time matches.

The repository also documents four measurement defects (a process-relative cross-process clock, a saturating replay speed, an asymmetric load generator, and a concurrency axis that was secretly a throughput axis), each of which reversed the apparent winner before correction.

Raw StatsBomb event JSONs are intentionally excluded and are re-fetchable from a pinned upstream commit via scripts/fetch_statsbomb_events.sh. See README.md and reproducibility/ for the full protocol.
